title: GTA 6 Rumour: PC Port Could Arrive in Early 2027
description: According to a new report from GamesBeat, GTA 6 might break Rockstar's tradition by releasing on PC in the first quarter of 2027, just months after PS5.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Rumour Points to a Surprisingly Fast PC Port in 2027

For years, Rockstar Games has been well known for prioritizing console platforms for its major video game releases. Players on personal computers have historically had to wait many months, or even years, before experiencing these massive open-world titles on their platform of choice. However, if a new report is accurate, GTA 6 might completely break that long-standing rule.

### What the Latest Report Suggests

According to information shared by GamesBeat and highlighted by Push Square, the highly anticipated open-world game is currently slated to come to PC in the **first quarter of 2027**. This timeline places the PC release just a few months following its initial debut on the PlayStation 5.

Should this report prove to be accurate, it would represent a massive shift in Rockstar's traditional release window strategy, drastically shortening the gap between console launches and PC availability for the studio's flagship franchise.

### Looking Back at Rockstar's Tradition

Traditionally, Rockstar Games focuses its initial development and marketing efforts on console ecosystems, allowing the studio to maximize optimization and launch sales on platforms like PlayStation and Xbox. PC versions have historically followed much later as a secondary wave of development. Shortening this window to just a few months would break records for the studio in terms of platform expansion speed.

### Editor's Take

(Unconfirmed rumor) While the prospect of playing GTA 6 on PC so soon after the PS5 launch is exciting, players should take this report with a grain of salt until an official announcement is made by Rockstar Games. Given the immense scale of the game, a fast turnaround is ambitious, but it could signal a major shift in the developer's multi-platform strategy.
